title: The CM-aGPi Network in the Generation of Tics in Tourette Syndrome.
design: Repeated CM and aGPi intracranial recordings, six TS participants with severe treatment-resistant tics, nine monthly visits; no stimulation during recordings.
original_summary: Low-frequency power and pallido-thalamic coherence differed between tic and symptom-free recording states. Within-person association identifies a candidate signal; it does not demonstrate causal tic generation, reliable clinical prediction, treatment benefit or disease modification.
population_limit: Age distribution not verified; do not label an adult-only cohort or extrapolate across severity. Six implanted participants are not nine independent cohorts or repeated-visit sample sizes.
full_text_status: Abstract only; public metadata and abstract inspected transiently.
cohort_deduplication: Absent from main ledger and exact-PMID GitHub code search. Same-participant overlap with other DBS reports remains unresolved; do not pool as an independent cohort.
correction_check: No linked correction/retraction in this EFetch snapshot; not full Crossmark clearance.
next_verification: Check licensed full-text eligibility, ages, clinical-trial identifiers and overlap with prior DBS cohorts before a bounded mechanism analysis.
